samples.text: The first signal was a ticket: INC0080099 opened at priority P2 against inventory-valuation. Triage started from the infrastructure, on the working assumption that the overnight platform had dropped data before the valuation run began. That assumption shaped the first part of the response, and in hindsight it cost time. The line of enquiry closed only when someone read the logs instead of reasoning about them: ERP logs show no interruption during the valuation window. With the platform cleared, attention moved to the inputs, and the reference data became the focus. The stale code mapping was found there, the valuation was rerun against corrected codes, and the status changed later the same day: Asset valuation completed. Two points follow from that sequence. First, the wrong theory was reasonable on the information available at the start, but it was never tested against the evidence until well into the incident. A log check

For the cluster finance partner, this is a utilisation question rather than a recovery question. The cluster used more of its cost budget than its income justified, and the overrun is not explained by volume, since funding came in on plan. The useful next step is to identify which programmes carried the additional cost in the month and whether those costs were planned work brought forward or genuine overspend. Work brought forward will unwind in later periods, while overspend will not. I would ask the partner to return that split before the next close, with commitments for the coming month tested against the budgeted cost ratio. Until that analysis is available, the cluster's position should be read as on plan for funding but outside plan for cost control.
